games.title: Assassin's Creed Valhalla
games.note: A Viking raider settles in ninth-century England and builds up a village.

games.title: Skull and Bones
games.note: An online pirate game announced in 2017 that went through years of delays before launching in 2024.

games.title: Far Cry 5
games.note: Moved the series to rural Montana, where a doomsday cult has taken over a county.

games.title: Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor
games.note: Its Nemesis system gave orc captains names and memories; Warner Bros. was granted a US patent on it in 2021.

games.title: Middle-earth: Shadow of War
games.note: Extended the Nemesis system to fortress sieges and recruitable orc followers.

games.title: Spider-Man 2
games.note: The film tie-in where web lines attach to real buildings, letting you swing freely across Manhattan.

games.title: Sunset Overdrive
games.note: You grind rails, bounce off cars and wall-run across a city overrun by energy-drink mutants.

games.title: The Incredible Hulk: Ultimate Destruction
games.note: Let the Hulk climb any building and turn cars into weapons, such as metal fists.

games.title: Prototype
games.note: A shape-shifter absorbs people to take their looks and memories in an outbreak-stricken Manhattan.

games.title: Sly Cooper and the Thievius Raccoonus
games.note: A cel-shaded raccoon thief and his gang; the start of Sucker Punch's stealth platformer series.

games.title: inFAMOUS
games.note: A bike courier gains electric powers after a blast and chooses, mission by mission, to be a hero or a villain.

games.title: inFAMOUS Second Son
games.note: Set in Seattle, near Sucker Punch's home base, with powers like smoke and neon.

games.title: Tenchu: Stealth Assassins
games.note: A ninja stealth game with a grappling hook and a meter showing how aware nearby guards are.

games.title: Onimusha: Warlords
games.note: A samurai action game whose hero was modeled on the actor Takeshi Kaneshiro.

games.title: Killzone Shadow Fall
games.note: A PlayStation 4 launch game; its engine was later named Decima.

games.title: Dead Island
games.note: Known for a reverse-motion CGI trailer; you fight zombies on a resort island with crafted weapons.

games.title: Mirror's Edge
games.note: A first-person free-running game where red-highlighted objects show the runner's path across rooftops.

games.title: Dying Light
games.note: Free-running through a zombie-infested city; at night, tougher and faster monsters come out.

games.title: Dying Light 2 Stay Human
games.note: A larger city where players' choices hand districts to rival factions.

games.title: Dying Light: The Beast
games.note: Began as expansion content for Dying Light 2 and grew into a standalone game starring Kyle Crane.

games.title: Days Gone
games.note: A drifter biker in Oregon, where hordes of hundreds of infected swarm together.

games.title: Sea of Thieves
games.note: Its early design work was called 'Players Creating Stories Together'; crews share one ship and must coordinate sails and cannons.

games.title: Black Desert Online
games.note: A Korean MMO known for its detailed character creator and action combat.

games.title: Crimson Desert
games.note: Sold over 2 million copies within a day of its March 2026 launch, Pearl Abyss said.

games.title: Cyberpunk 2077
games.note: Sony pulled it from the PlayStation Store a week after launch because of bugs in the last-generation versions.

games.title: Cyberpunk 2020
games.note: The second edition of Mike Pondsmith's pen-and-paper RPG Cyberpunk, set in Night City.

games.title: Honkai Impact 3rd
games.note: miHoYo's mobile anime action game, released three years before Genshin Impact was announced.

links.took: Ubisoft Montreal's acrobatic climbing; the project began as a Prince of Persia spin-off.
links.added: Open historical cities, blending into crowds and a modern-day framing story.

src.t: Wikipedia: Assassin's Creed (video game); first pitched as Prince of Persia: Assassin

links.extra: Patrice Désilets, creative director of Sands of Time, also led Assassin's Creed.

links.took: The RPG-style open world, levels and gear of the rebooted series.
links.added: Viking raids, an upgradable home village and ninth-century England.

links.took: Ubisoft's large RPG open world and a home base you build up.
links.added: Feudal Japan with two playable heroes, a samurai and a shinobi, and changing seasons.

links.took: The naval combat Ubisoft Singapore built for Black Flag.
links.added: Online pirate ships for groups of players, without on-foot assassin missions.
links.extra: Ubisoft Singapore developed Black Flag's naval battles, and Skull and Bones grew from them.

links.took: Ubisoft Quebec's Greek setting and technology, from which the project grew.
links.added: Comic narration by Zeus and Prometheus, and puzzle vaults to solve.

links.took: Outposts, a charismatic villain and a large open world.
links.added: Rural Montana, recruitable companions and no radio towers to climb.

links.took: Climbing a tower to reveal the surrounding part of the map.
links.added: Radio towers on a tropical island, plus outposts to clear and animals to hunt.

src.t: Wikipedia: Open world (Assassin's Creed's tower mechanic reused in Far Cry and Watch Dogs)

links.took: Climbing towers to fill in the map, a habit Assassin's Creed popularized.
links.added: Towers that reveal terrain but not icons, leaving you to spot places yourself.

src.t: Wikipedia: Open world (lists Breath of the Wild among games using the tower mechanic)

links.extra: Nintendo has not named Assassin's Creed as an influence.

links.took: Free-flow counter-based combat and stealth takedowns.
links.added: The Nemesis system: orc captains who remember you, rise in rank and seek revenge.
links.extra: Monolith said the Arkham games inspired its stealth and free-flow combat.

links.took: Climbing, open-world movement and stealth kills from above.
links.added: Tolkien's Mordor and procedurally named orc rivals with their own grudges.

src.t: Wikipedia: Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor (cites Matt Miller, Game Informer)

links.extra: Game Informer named Assassin's Creed and Batman: Arkham as the game's inspirations.

links.took: The Nemesis system and Arkham-style combat.
links.added: Fortress sieges and orc followers who can betray you.

links.took: Web-swinging that attaches to real buildings across an open Manhattan.
links.added: Smoother swinging and wall-running, gadget combat and an older Peter Parker.
links.extra: A popularized mechanic, not a stated influence: EGMNow found the new swinging more streamlined than Spider-Man 2's.

links.took: Insomniac's fast open-city traversal, which Ted Price saw as a base to build on.
links.added: Web-swinging, a licensed Spider-Man story and Marvel's New York.

links.took: A superhero game built on rhythmic brawling, gadgets and stealth takedowns.
links.added: An open New York to swing through, plus Peter Parker's home life.

src.t: Wikipedia: Marvel's Spider-Man (Marvel Games' Jay Ong; VentureBeat and Game Informer reviews)

links.extra: Marvel Games wanted a series that could 'beat Arkham', and reviewers compared the two.

links.took: Free movement through an open city as a superhero, popularized by Spider-Man 2.
links.added: Climbing any building, giant leaps and turning cars into weapons.

links.took: Radical's open-city superpower play: running up buildings, huge leaps and smashing.
links.added: A shape-shifter who absorbs people, and an outbreak spreading through Manhattan.
links.extra: Often called a spiritual successor to Ultimate Destruction.

links.took: The same studio, who wanted something 'brazen and loud' after six years of stealth games.
links.added: An open city, electric superpowers and choices between hero and villain.

links.took: An open city to roam; the team pictured themselves as superheroes in Liberty City.
links.added: Superpowers instead of cars and guns, and a city that reacts to good or evil.

links.took: Moving freely around a city and answering random calls for help between missions.
links.added: Electric powers, grinding along power lines and a moral choice system.

links.took: Open-city superpowers and the hero-or-villain karma system.
links.added: Several switchable powers like smoke and neon, set in Seattle on PlayStation 4.

links.took: Sucker Punch's open-world tools, with many particle effects carried over.
links.added: Swapped neon superpowers for a quiet, painterly feudal Japan.
links.extra: Creative director Jason Connell said the art team struggled to leave inFAMOUS's 'punk rock' look behind.

links.took: Minimal on-screen guidance and wide, sparse landscapes.
links.added: A guiding wind you summon with a swipe on the controller's touchpad.
links.extra: The developers said Shadow of the Colossus inspired the wind-based guidance.

links.took: A clean, minimalist look for a large open landscape.
links.added: Feudal Japanese fields and forests, samurai duels and the 1274 Mongol invasion.

links.took: Horseback travel across a large open landscape.
links.added: Samurai sword combat, standoffs and a wind that points the way.
links.extra: Wikipedia lists Red Dead Redemption and Karateka among cited inspirations, without details.

links.took: Cinematic one-on-one duels in a feudal Japanese setting.
links.added: Combat stances, standoffs and an open island to free from invaders.
links.extra: Cited without details; Karateka was made by Jordan Mechner in 1984.

links.took: Ninja tools and items, many of which were based on Tenchu's.
links.added: A samurai who becomes the stealthy 'Ghost', mixing open duels with assassinations.

links.took: The idea of fighting as either an honorable samurai or a shadowy 'ghost'.
links.added: A historical Mongol invasion and a large island to roam on horseback.

links.took: How densely to fill a large open world, studied from Skyrim's structure.
links.added: Robot dinosaurs to hunt with bows and traps in a post-apocalyptic tribal world.

links.took: Emergent RPG freedom that lets players go beyond what designers planned.
links.added: Machine-hunting tactics, tearing off parts and a mystery about the old world.

links.took: Guerrilla's engine, later named Decima, built for Killzone Shadow Fall.
links.added: Open-world streaming, nature and machine creatures in place of linear shooter levels.

links.took: Guerrilla's Decima engine, shared with Kojima Productions.
links.added: Delivery treks across empty landscapes, linking players' structures online.

links.took: Hideo Kojima's team and the open-world, systems-heavy design of MGS V.
links.added: Walking, balance and cargo weight as the core challenge, with shared online structures.

links.took: Techland's first-person melee combat, weapon crafting and zombie-filled open maps.
links.added: Free-running across rooftops and a day-night cycle that makes nights deadly.

links.took: First-person parkour; the team first aimed for a system like Mirror's Edge's.
links.added: Parkour in an open, zombie-filled city, with a grappling hook and night chases.

links.took: Parkour, crafted melee weapons and dangerous nights.
links.added: A bigger city, a paraglider and story choices that change districts.

links.took: Kyle Crane, the first game's hero, and its parkour combat.
links.added: A beast mode that turns Crane's infection into raw strength, in a new valley.

links.took: Cinematic storytelling that Bend wanted to bring from linear games like Uncharted.
links.added: An open Oregon wilderness, a motorbike to maintain and giant hordes of infected.
links.extra: The source names the Uncharted series rather than one game.

links.took: Unscripted encounters between strangers that become stories players retell.
links.added: Pirate crews sharing one ship, with no permanent loss of everything when you die.

src.t: Joe Neate (Rare), GamesTM interview, via GamingBolt

links.extra: Neate played the DayZ mod once and called its player encounters a massive inspiration.

links.took: A community that makes players famous through their own videos and stories.
links.added: Pirate reputations earned at sea, with cosmetic rewards instead of power.

src.t: Joe Neate (Rare), GamesTM interview, via Wccftech

links.took: Pearl Abyss's technology and world; it was first planned as a Black Desert Online prequel.
links.added: A single-player action adventure set in its own continent, Pywel.

links.took: CD Projekt Red's REDengine and its story-driven open-world quest design.
links.added: A first-person view, cyberware upgrades and the futuristic Night City.

links.took: Mike Pondsmith's Night City, factions and cyberware from the tabletop RPG.
links.added: A first-person open-world video game set 57 years later.

src.t: Wikipedia: Cyberpunk 2077 (based on Cyberpunk 2020; Pondsmith consulted)

links.took: miHoYo's 3D anime art, action combat and gacha business model.
links.added: A large open world to climb and glide over, with element-combo combat.

links.took: Data on building a world at huge scale, which Nintendo researched in Skyrim.
links.added: Climbing anything, gliding and physics and chemistry puzzles across Hyrule.
links.extra: In 2016 Aonuma told Game Informer Skyrim was not an inspiration; in 2017 he said the team studied it for data.

links.took: Open-ended freedom to solve problems using the world's own rules.
links.added: Physics, fire, wind and metal that interact, inside a Zelda adventure.

src.t: Hidemaro Fujibayashi, Edge interview, via Siliconera, Mar 2017

links.extra: Fujibayashi: 'I was rather inspired by playing Minecraft and Terraria.'

links.took: Open-ended exploration where players set their own goals and gather materials.
links.added: A 3D Hyrule with climbing, gliding, cooking and shrines.

src.t: Hidemaro Fujibayashi, Edge interview, via Siliconera, Mar 2017
